clue.text: Elgar's regal composition

parts.note: the letters of the composer's name, rearranged or composed anew, spell the word regal, so this is a description of a letter-shuffle

explanation.surface: A stately piece of music by the English composer Edward Elgar.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a royal march by Elgar, but ELGAR and REGAL use exactly the same five letters, so the 'composition' is a rearrangement of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearrangement of one word's letters into another word is the name for exactly this kind of wordplay.

clue.text: Person making charges in account about drug addict

parts.note: C is circa, meaning about
a user is slang for a drug taker

explanation.surface: An accuser is involved in a drug addict's financial affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who brings charges against another is their accuser, a direct description.

clue.text: Gathers a thousand animals together

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
asses are donkeys

explanation.surface: A herd of a thousand beasts collects together.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to collect or gather up, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Crest where soldiers possibly dig in

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes inside the soldiers' abbreviation

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, British Army soldiers

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A hilltop where troops might entrench themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The soldiers are the Royal Engineers (RE), a common crossword convention; 'possibly' scrambles DIG to IDG, which they enclose, matching the surface picture of troops digging in.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the crest or top line of a hill or roof.

clue.text: Being malicious, the German newspaper leader wasn't straight

parts.note: mean can mean spiteful or malicious
der is a German word for the
ED is the editor, who heads a newspaper

explanation.surface: A spiteful German editor proved to be crooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A river that meanders winds about, so it did not run straight.

clue.text: A little crawler going round quietly to investigate

indicators.note: the creature's name surrounds the musical letter, wrapping round it

parts.note: an insect is a small creeping creature
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Someone examines a tiny bug as it circles softly.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something closely is to look into it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Not all but certain currencies suffer

indicators.note: only part of the phrase is used, so the answer lies within it

explanation.surface: Some currencies take a loss.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss is to suffer or sustain it.

clue.text: A foreigner without money — he's choked off

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, the foreigner surrounds the money letter

parts.note: a stranger is an outsider or foreigner
L is the pound sign, money

explanation.surface: An alien with no cash is a man silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside here; 'choked off' plays on choking someone to death.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler chokes victims, so he cuts off their breath, a playful description.

clue.text: Chapter and verse after record is set

indicators.note: after places the poem following the earlier pieces

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
taken as written
an ode is a verse composition

explanation.surface: A section and a poem come after a disc is fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: An episode is one instalment of a serial, like a chapter of a story.

clue.text: Everybody gets involved in the trial that's most preposterous

indicators.note: the word for everybody goes into the trial word

parts.note: a test is a trial
all means everybody

explanation.surface: Everyone is drawn into a ridiculous court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is far-fetched, so the tallest is the most implausible.

clue.text: Among American secret agents there's praise for this woman

indicators.note: the word for praise sits among the letters of the agency's initials

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
to laud is to praise

explanation.surface: A woman is admired by US spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudia is a female first name, so it identifies a woman.

clue.text: Welcoming a non-alcoholic drink

definitions.meaning: a sweet fruit concentrate diluted with water, such as lime juice

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both warmly friendly and a diluted fruit syrup drink, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Second exercise in part responsible for a hold-up

indicators.note: the two short pieces go inside the verb meaning part

parts.note: to sunder is to part or split
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A brief bout of training somewhere causes a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold-up' suggests a robbery or a delay, but here it is literal: a garter that holds up a stocking, or braces holding up trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A garter strap or braces keep stockings or trousers from falling, literally holding them up.

clue.text: She was very tearful in retiring with honour

indicators.note: something retiring goes back, so the little word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A woman wept as she stepped down with a royal decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: Niobe in Greek myth wept endlessly for her slain children and was turned into a weeping rock.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the mother whose children were killed wept until she became stone, the archetype of grief.

clue.text: Is still taken by those playing snooker

definitions.meaning: cue supports used in snooker for long shots, which players pick up

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for staying still and the name of the snooker cue supports.

clue.text: This individual's game is brilliant

definitions.meaning: a single gemstone, a diamond set on its own

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a one-player card game and a single diamond set alone in a ring.

clue.text: Don't forget about raise!

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to raise money is to collect it

explanation.surface: A reminder to remember a pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' looks like a pay rise but is the verb, as in raising funds.
explanation.definitionFit: To remember is to call back to mind, so not forgetting is a synonym.

clue.text: Many tots need correction, it's argued

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, many

indicators.note: correction implies the letters must be put right

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Lots of children need to be disciplined, it's said.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correction' turns TOTSNEED into ONTESTED, placed after C.
explanation.definitionFit: A contested point is one that has been argued over or disputed.

clue.text: Having too much on, even a lord can go to pieces

indicators.note: going to pieces breaks the phrase apart for reassembly

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Under too much pressure, even an aristocrat may crack.
explanation.definitionFit: Overladen means carrying too heavy a load, i.e. burdened with too much.

clue.text: A man shunned for striking players

parts.note: workers on strike are out
the cast are the actors in a production

explanation.surface: An actor is ostracised for walking out with the troupe.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcast is a person rejected and avoided by society.

clue.text: Issue Number 1 with current backup

indicators.note: backup in a down clue means the pieces read upward, backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a tide is a current

explanation.surface: First edition with a current backup copy.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue of a newspaper or magazine is one printing of it.

clue.text: Spoke repeatedly

parts.note: spoke read as a noun, a wheel rod or a line from a circle's centre, in plural form

explanation.surface: Someone talked again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spoke' looks like the past tense of speak; it is the noun, and 'repeatedly' makes it plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines from a circle's centre to its edge, like wheel spokes, are its plural geometric lines.

clue.text: Only for motorists creating row about split

indicators.note: the noise word wraps about the split word

parts.note: din is a loud row or noise
to rive is to split

explanation.surface: Drivers alone are causing an argument about a split.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-in cinema or restaurant serves customers who stay in their cars.

clue.text: Stylish file one really doesn't appreciate

parts.note: in means fashionable
to grate is to rasp, like using a file

explanation.surface: A fancy nail file is something one dislikes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingrate is an ungrateful person, one who fails to show thanks.

clue.text: Misrepresent a pitiable waif

definitions.meaning: Oliver, the workhouse orphan in Dickens's novel, bears this surname

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to distort, and it is also the surname of Dickens's poor orphan Oliver.

clue.text: Watches a fly moving up and down

parts.note: sees means watches
taken as written
to wing is to fly

explanation.surface: Someone observes an insect bobbing up and down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the insect but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw goes up and down, so the participle means rising and falling alternately.

clue.text: Pole was clearly distressed, but cleaned up

parts.note: S is the South Pole
wept means cried, showing distress plainly

explanation.surface: A Polish person cried but tidied up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person, but it is a geographic pole.
explanation.definitionFit: To have swept is to have cleaned with a broom.

clue.text: Confess to being mad about it

indicators.note: about here means turned around, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: fodder taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Owning up to being crazy about something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confess to' is the definition, and 'about' is the scramble signal rather than 'concerning': it makes ADM from MAD, with IT added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to confess to it.

clue.text: Seen as a fault in the Orient — and stupid

parts.note: taken as written
a sin is a moral fault
taken as written
E is east, the Orient

explanation.surface: Something regarded in the East as a failing and also foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means donkey-like in foolishness, a synonym for silly.

clue.text: Irritation shown with a painter's technique

parts.note: temper here means a bad mood or irritation
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist's method causes annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is painting with pigment bound in egg yolk, an artistic method.

clue.text: Set it in maybe, but no more than the minimum

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets something in place, keeping it to a bare minimum.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiniest means smallest of all, which amounts to the very minimum.

clue.text: A letter about holiday accommodation should ease tension

definitions.note: read as a noun phrase, an easing of tension

indicators.note: the spelt-out letter wraps about the camping shelter

parts.note: dee is the spelt-out name of the letter D
a tent is camping accommodation for a holiday

explanation.surface: A note about a camping holiday is meant to calm things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ease' is read as a noun here: an easing of tension, the diplomatic sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, from French, names a relaxation of strained relations between nations.
